title.narrative: Improved policies and programmes to ensure safe and healthy working conditions

description.narrative: Recognizing the importance of safety and health in the workplace, as a critical component of the decent work agenda, the Government of Somalia called on ILO’s support to elaborate a national policy for a comprehensive intervention. It is affirmed by the tripartite constituents that ensuring and maintaining safety and health in workplaces is one of the avenues of increasing longevity of life, employee productivity and organizational competitiveness. The new policy is anticipated to replace the weak legal, policy and institutional framework in Somalia for ensuring safety and health in workplaces. The NDP 2020 – 2024 notes that the lack of building standards and health and safety regulation leaves a risk of poor-quality work, high-cost maintenance and injury compensation that could create disincentives for The stabilization of the political situation has allowed the ILO to relaunch the process of elaboration of the OSH policy under the CPO 127, with the national partners in late 2022. Within the PDSP project, a tripartite taskforce was constituted to monitor the process of implementing an OSH systemic approach in Somalia. The strategy followed included building the capacity of the task force members on OSH strategic approach, hiring a national consultant and undertaking close supervision by the ILO OSH specialists based in Algiers and HQ. In September 2022, a tripartite workshop was held allowing the presentation of the OSH profile to the tripartite committee and the development of the first OSH policy and program. During 2023, MOLSA has been involved in a process of validation of the OSH policy that has been endorsed by the Somalia's Council of Ministers. The seal of approval was granted on 18 January 2024. During the biennium 24-25, under the CPO ILO will continue supporting MOLSA in the development of OSH system in Somalia at 2 levels.
